title: Introduce trace-sink negotiation protocol to offload sampling during sustained bursts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: During sustained request bursts the hotpath allocation and CPU cost of span encoding and enrichment for tracing becomes a significant portion of the inference path CPU (esp. gateway and sidecars). Existing prefilter and deferred-emit approaches reduce cost but still require the caller to perform decision logic and occasional costly encoding when signals flip.

Goal: Implement a lightweight negotiation protocol between edge proxies/clients and trace sinks (collectors) so that collectors can advertise short-lived acceptance tokens and granular backpressure hints. Clients use these hints to strictly avoid heavy span encoding and metadata enrichment unless the sink signals acceptance for that trace window. This reduces hotpath allocations and CPU without losing the ability to capture tails when capacity allows.

Scope: protocol design, runtime client changes (gateway/sidecar), collector (sink) changes, metrics/telemetry changes, compatibility mode, rollout/canary plan and dashboards. Not in scope: full revamp of ingestion pipeline upstream compressors.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiation token exchange implemented in gateway sidecar and collector (v1 lightweight tokens)
Hotpath CPU allocations for gateway reduced >=15% in steady-state bursts in our benchmark cluster
No increase in end-to-end 99th percentile latency attributable to negotiation (measured across canary)
Fallback: when collector does not support negotiation, behavior remains unchanged
Instrumentation: new metrics for token-issuance-rate, token-acceptance-rate, client-defer-rate available in Grafana
tasks: Write design doc and protocol spec (Confluence)
Implement token API in collector (HTTP/2 endpoint)
Add client-side token cache and decision fastpath in gateway/sidecar
End-to-end integration test including simulated burst scenarios
Canary rollout and monitor for regressions
comments: 2025-02-14 | Aisha Kapoor: Created initial ticket after oncall spike where gateway CPU rose 30% and trace pipeline showed large encoding tail. Linked preliminary perf notes and allocation profiles.

2025-02-15 | Miguel Torres: Did tech spike — implemented a prototype token cache in gateway. Observed 18% CPU reduction and 38% fewer allocations for span encoder in a 10k qps sustained workload. Results and script: https://gist.github.com/miguel/negotiation-spike

2025-02-17 | Priya Mehta (Observability Lead): Design review feedback — ensure tokens are bearer-only short-lived (TTL <= 5s) and authentication uses existing mTLS between components. Also call out rehydration behavior for cold-start traces.

2025-02-19 | Miguel Torres: Updated design to include exponential backoff on token renewal and a soft-fallback where clients emit a minimal 'skeleton' span when tokens absent (to preserve sampling signals upstream). Added draft API contract to Confluence.

2025-02-21 | Security (Jamal Reed): Security review notes — require proof-of-possession for tokens to avoid token reuse across tenants; recommend signed token (HMAC) with per-collector key rotation. Marking security_review_required=true.

2025-02-24 | UX/Console (Ellen Park): Dashboard proposal accepted; added panels for token-issuance-rate, client-defer-rate, and collector-drop-rate. Requested runbook entries for triage when tokens are unexpectedly low.

2025-02-25 | Miguel Torres: Opened GitHub PR for collector changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-collector/pull/142 (draft). Benchmark results attached in PR description. Need infra help to provision canary cluster for real workload testing.

2025-02-26 | Oncall (Luca Romano): Noted an edge case where token churn correlates with collector GC pause; added dependency to scheduling and memory tuning task. Added ENG-509999 as follow-up for GC mitigation in collector.
